- 构建模式: full（full=无头 wineboot 完整 hive；auto=失败降级骨架；skeleton=纯骨架）

  - `*-with-wine.tar.gz` —— 槽位树布局：App「Wine 管理 → 从本地安装」（prefix-pack 自动随槽位落位，成为该槽位一级模板来源）
  - `*-with-wine-rootfs.tar.gz` — data/data 全路径：终端 `linbox-container install-wine <包>` 一键落位

releases.name: LinBox Bionic Box64 v0.4.4 (aarch64)
releases.body:
LinBox bionic rootfs 专用 Box64（aarch64 / NDK bionic 链接 / -DANDROID=ON / ARM_DYNAREC）

- bionic ELF（PT_INTERP=/system/bin/linker64），与 rootfs 内
  wine / mesa / pulseaudio 等二进制同链同形态；box64 本体零
  glibc 依赖
- 完整安装集（不再只有单个 box64 执行文件）：
  `usr/local/bin/box64` + `usr/bin/box64` PATH 入口链接
  + `usr/lib/box64-x86_64-linux-gnu/libc++_shared.so`
  （上游 ANDROID 模式配套，被仿真 x86_64 程序的 C++ 标准库）
  + `usr/etc/box64.box64rc`（系统级调优开关）
  + `usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/`（`ld-linux-aarch64.so.1`
  私有加载器与 aarch64 glibc 运行库 —— glibc 形态 box64
  与 rootfs 内 glibc 二进制的运行层）
  + `usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/`（被仿真 x86_64 程序的
  glibc 运行库，box64 经 BOX64_LD_LIBRARY_PATH 查找）
- 手动安装: 解包 `linbox-box64-*.tar.gz` 至 /（data/data/com.linbox/...
  自动就位），或 `linbox-container install-box64 <tar.gz|URL>`
- 安装后 linbox-container 自动探测 /usr/local/bin/box64
- 用途: 在 aarch64 设备上运行 x86_64 Wine（backend=box64）；
  v0.4.4 为 hangover-11.16 官方配套版本（错配可致 wineboot SEH 级联崩溃）
- 注意: 与完整 rootfs 包（build-bionic-rootfs）同源 —— rootfs 已内置
  同款 box64 与配套文件，单独升级时才需要本包

ares v148 has now been released.

This release includes big improvements to a number of ares cores. Highlights include rewrites to the N64 CPU & RSP JITs resulting in significant performance gains across the N64 library, additional implementation & accuracy improvements to the PlayStation core, fixes to the GBA core, and support for the Famicom data recorder & Dendy. 

Additionally, there have been many updates to the core ares application across all platforms. Per-core input configuration has been added, updated video, audio, & input drivers are available, bug fixes, additional options have been added, and core dependencies have been updated. 

Since v147, 20 contributors have created 300 commits to the ares codebase.

As always, if you wish to see the full changelog in a per-commit format along with their authors, you can do so on GitHub [here](https://github.com/ares-emulator/ares/compare/v147...v148).

releases.name: Cmod Progress Update - December 2025: What's next?
releases.body:
Hello!

It's been a little while, so I thought I would just give a small update on project status. 

- Winlator Cmod development continues!
- My focus on next release will either be mostly QoL. This means addressing long standing bug fixes, but more importantly, **merging and crediting improvements from other forks of Cmod from trusted developers.** Primarily I'll be focused on:
- Fixing dynamic package name paths for the gamepad implementation so that name can be changed, such as adding a ludashi benchmark version with the SDL joystick native controller support.
- Input control / touch screen control bindings bug fixes
- Minor UI improvements and enhancements
- Updating all drivers, Fex, Box64, and graphics Wrapper, following Pipetto-Crypto's advice when it comes to Streamlining and avoiding feature creep (...and avoiding pure AI code slop). 
- Improve ALSA-Reflector so audio stops cutting out after 15 minutes unless you switch to headphones.

releases.name: Winlator Cmod v13.1.1
releases.body:
_Minor update v13.1.1 fixed custom icons, default renderer, and warning prompt handling on new installs_ 

------------------------------

-   **`evshim` Rewrite:** The entire controller shim (`libevshim.so`) has been rewritten, **completely eliminating the use of shared memory (`mmap`)**, resulting in a massive reduction in CPU overhead and a significant performance boost, especially on lower-end devices. Box64 3.2 and 3.6 are now compatible, and have been restored.

-   **ALSA-Reflector Improved** The pacer's ring buffer and reconnection logic have been refined, expect better performance and reliability.

-   **Universal CPU Overhead Reduction:** I've gone through the code to find and eliminate performance bottlenecks, once again, big thanks to @Pipetto-crypto as always for the guidance and his improvements to the Graphics Wrapper. 

### ✨ New Feature: VkBasalt Integration

-   **Per-Shortcut Sharpening & Effects:** Thanks to @Pipetto-crypto You can now enable VkBasalt on a per-shortcut basis to apply CAS and DLS to your games.

### 🐞 Stability & Bug Fixes:

This update includes a huge number of fixes for a smoother experience.

releases.name: Winlator Cmod v13: The Controller Revolution is Here! (And much more...)
releases.body: The wait is over. After months of work the next major evolution of Winlator Cmod has arrived. I teased that a controller revolution was coming, but the reality is so much bigger. This isn't just an update; it's a top-to-bottom overhaul focused on bringing a native, seamless gaming experience to your device. This release is the culmination of a journey, and I'm proud to share it with you. ✨ What's New in Cmod v13 ✨ -------------------------- ### 🎮 The Controller Revolution: Native Gamepad Support is Here! The old input methods are gone (sorta), replaced by a completely new, from-the-ground-up controller implementation built on a native SDL2 backend. - **Native XInput & DInput Support:** No more switching settings per game! Controllers are now treated like real controllers. If it works on a PC, it should just work here. - **Multiplayer (Up to 4 Players!):** You heard that right. Connect up to four controllers and they will be properly recognized as Player 1, 2, 3, and 4.

Are you Ready 2 Rumble? Or vibrate? 

Do you have friends? Like, up to 4?

new update fellas:D this one brings more optimization and bug fixes

Mobile Odyssey 0.4 (beta)

There are two APKs. odyssey-0.4.apk is for most phones (ARMv8.2 or newer). odyssey-0.4-armv8.0.apk is for phones with older processors (ARMv8.0 or 8.1), and the launcher tells you if you need it. Both install over 0.3, and your save and settings stay

added Frame generation: makes an extra frame after each real one, so the game shows 60 frames a second while running at 30. It looks smoother but with the latency of 30. You can set it to Off, On or Auto in the launcher or the in-game menu. Auto only turns it on when your phone can't hold 60 but can keep up with frame generation. The motion comes from the game's own camera and objects, so the extra frames line up well with the real ones. This ran pretty well for me but might be troublesome for older phones, so use Fast quality for it to run a bit better.

releases.name: beta 3.0
releases.body:
Beta 0.3

This update focuses on speed. On my Galaxy S24 Ultra (Snapdragon 8 Gen 3) Cascade now runs at about 58-60 fps, a pretty good improvement from about 44 in 0.2. On a tester’s Xiaomi with a Dimensity 8300 (Mali-G615) it runs at about 40 fps, fairly stable, with no graphical issues. Your results will likely be different, since it depends a lot on your phone.

What’s new:

Mali phones should see one of the biggest changes: the GPU doesnt sit idle waiting for the CPU anymore, so the game uses about 1 GB less memory now

A new “Preparing graphics” progress bar on game starts, instead of the frozen Joy-Con screen. (as always this will take a hot second if its your first launch, give it a minute to build the cache, and any launch after that should be MUCH faster.

the new Steady game speed:D, replacement of the original 30 fps option,now its  an option that keeps the game at normal speed at ANY fps below 60 fps. This means you can run the game at any fps and the game will NOT run in slow motion, as long as you enable it.
(its still recomended that you cap the fps to something you can consistantly hit)

releases.name: beta 0.2
releases.body:
the second release, big imrpvoement for the 60 fps mode, and Mali phones finally look right.

## Iron Lemon v0.2.0

The first Iron Lemon: Lemon's work on the original yuzu core, without Eden's changes, in an app of its own that installs next to Lemon. Same team, same key, a different core: if a game misbehaves in one, try the other.

This is a preview release. Lemon stays the main app; Iron Lemon's updates arrive as previews like this one.

### What's in it
- **Speed, Normal and Quality modes**: the whole emulator set up in one tap, also from the in-game menu and per game.
- **GPU accuracy in three plain levels**: Low, Normal and High (slow). Normal mode uses Normal.
- **Lemon FG** frame generation, quick saves, **Lemon Cheater**, cheat downloads and macros.
- **Online play on Nextendo Network.**
- **Lemon-Ade driver** built in and picked on Snapdragon from the first launch.
- **Mali GPUs**: BCn textures recompressed on the GPU, faster readback of GPU results.
- **Import** saves, keys and firmware from Lemon or another emulator.
- **Updates inside the app**, a What's new card, and an **Iron Lemon Spoofed** variant.
- A warning when your keys are older than your firmware.

## Lemon-Project v1.5.0

One Lemon for everyone: three modes replace the separate builds, the GPU is emulated on its own thread by default, and a round of fixes from your logs. Welcome to **rcssf**, the newest member of Team Lemon.

### New
- **Speed, Normal and Quality modes**, the first card in Settings. One choice sets resolution, filtering, anti-aliasing, GPU mode and shader building. - **Lemon Lite & Spoofed becomes Lemon Spoofed**: plain Lemon under a benchmark app's package name, with no settings of its own. Lite & Spoofed installs update into it with their data.

# Hokkaido 0.7.0

The biggest Hokkaido release so far: a second engine. Next to Hokkaido's emulator, the APK now carries [Banana Native](https://git.eden-emu.dev/moceure/BananaNative), which runs a Switch 2 game's code natively on the phone and draws its graphics through Vulkan. You choose the engine per game, and Banana Native runs behind Hokkaido's own screens, with Hokkaido's GPU driver, saves and settings.

Tested on a Samsung Galaxy S26 (Exynos 2600, Xclipse 960, 12 GB), a Galaxy S24 (Exynos 2400, Xclipse 940, 8 GB) and a Galaxy S25 (Snapdragon 8 Elite, Adreno 830, 12 GB), all on Android 17.

**Updating:** install the APK over 0.6.x. Your games, saves and settings stay. Every game keeps running on the Hokkaido engine unless Banana Native has a playable profile for it (see Auto below), and you can switch any game back in Game properties.

## Getting started with Banana Native

1. **GPU driver.** On an Xclipse GPU (Exynos), install a custom RADV driver in Hokkaido's GPU driver manager, globally or for the game. Banana Native uses the same driver as Hokkaido.

# Hokkaido 0.6.5

Tested on a Samsung Galaxy S26 (Exynos 2600, Xclipse 960, 12 GB) and, for the first time, a Galaxy S25 (Snapdragon 8 Elite, Adreno 830, 12 GB), both on Android 17. The performance work tested on the S26's Exynos carries over well to Snapdragon.

- **Fast Fusion** now gets past its title screen and into races, but at low frame rates (the game runs in slow motion) and with a shimmering image. Before, it crashed right after the splash screen on every phone tested: at 0.5x resolution, render targets were freed while a cached scaling helper still used them.

- **Speed and memory** (upstream)
  - GPU address space is reused and given back when the allocator runs out.
  - Command list copies are reused instead of made again.
  - Occlusion query lookups, frees and locks are cheaper.
  - Game file sections open when they are first used.
  - Memory write traps skip the texture cache on pages that hold no texture.

# Hokkaido 0.6.4

Tested on a Samsung Galaxy S26 (Exynos 2600, Xclipse 960, 12 GB) and a Galaxy S24 (Exynos 2400, Xclipse 940, 8 GB), both on Android 17.

## Highlights

- **Game compatibility** (upstream)
  - A texture slot that is still empty when a shader is built now compiles as a 2D texture. Upstream this fixed Pokémon Legends Z-A's blank screen.
  - Shader translation no longer runs out of stack on Kirby Air Riders' loops.
  - More shaders translate: shifts with a uniform shift amount (SHF), and more texture gather and call forms.
  - Ocarina of Time 1.0 (without the update) works with the "No Sharpening" anti-aliasing setting.
- **Snapdragon:** Adreno's early depth test (LRZ) is turned off where it drew wrong, on Qualcomm's own driver (upstream).
- **Memory** (upstream)
  - ASTC textures with uneven mip levels stay compressed on phones and other GPUs with shared or small memory.
  - A new buffer no longer joins a large buffer it only shares a page with. Upstream this caused slowdowns and a crash on Yoshi's book pages.
  - Memory hints skip placeholder addresses.
- **Stability** (upstream)
  - Closing a game while its shaders load no longer hangs, and the next launch works.

releases.name: Dual-Screen 3.0.2 (based on Dusklight v2.0.0)
releases.body:
Restores compatibility with third-party native mods. If mods failed to load, or loaded and then force-closed the game, this is the fix.

### Fixed

* **Mods failed to load with "Unknown mod load failure".** ([#6](https://github.com/igawa6/dusklight/issues/6))

  Adding the companion's slot I/II buttons pushed `BTN_R` to `1 << 8` and widened `daAlink_c::itemTriggerCheck` / `itemButtonCheck` from `u8` to `u16`. That changes the mangled names, so mods built against upstream Dusklight could not resolve them and failed at `dlopen`. The upstream symbols are re-exported as forwarders that translate the button numbering as well as the width — upstream's `BTN_B` is `BTN_S2` here, so widening alone would have routed a sword check to a slot button.

  Measured against three mods: only 2 of 842, 762 and 55 game-symbol imports were unresolved.

* **The game force-closed when a loaded mod ran.**

releases.name: Dual-Screen 3.0.1 (based on Dusklight v2.0.0)
releases.body:
Patch release for **Dual-Screen 3.0**. No gameplay or dual-screen changes — the native code is identical to 3.0.

### Fixed

* **Cosmetics, Luau Support and Randomizer were missing from the Android build.** ([#6](https://github.com/igawa6/dusklight/issues/6))

  The Android CMake presets listed only the `dusklight` target, so the `dusklight_mods` aggregate target never ran and `bundled_mods/` was never produced. Gradle packs that directory into `assets/mods`, so the APK shipped with no bundled mod packages at all. Mods that depend on the Luau runtime could not load either.

  All three packages are now present: `cosmetics`, `luau_runtime` and `randomizer`.

  CI was never affected — `build.yml` builds `dusklight_mods` as its own explicit `--target` step. This only broke preset-driven local builds.

releases.name: v2.5.0
releases.body:
## Highlights

- **Disk images are kept unmodified with a save directory.** With `-saveDir`, what the software writes goes to an overlay file there and the image is only read. Overlays store only the tracks or blocks written and are tied to a checksum of their image. This also makes writable the disks that could not be written before: inside a zip or gzip, loaded from a URL, or embedded in the executable.
- **DOS 3.3 boots in five seconds.** The Disk II motor keeps turning for about a second after the drive is turned off, like the 556 timer of the real controller, and the data latch no longer reads the same nibble twice. DOS no longer waits for the motor on every access: a DOS 3.3 boot takes 5.4 million cycles instead of 36 million.
- **A libretro core** runs izapple2 inside RetroArch and the other libretro frontends, with diskette swapping from M3U playlists and saves as overlays. It is built from source and is not in the release archives. See [the libretro page](https://github.com/ivanizag/izapple2/blob/master/doc/frontend_libretro.md) and [the Mac guide](https://github.com/ivanizag/izapple2/blob/master/doc/frontend_libretro_macos.md).

# RMG-K v0.9.16

## Jump into games already in progress
- **Late join:** if a match has an open seat, you can join the room mid-game. The host clicks **Add to Game** and you're in after a pause of a few seconds. Nobody else's game restarts.
- **Rejoin after a drop:** if you get disconnected, the host can add you back the same way.
- **Start solo:** hosts can start a match alone and add friends as they show up.
- Hosts can turn late join on or off for each room.

## Save files
- Matches now start from the host's save file, so everyone has the same unlocks.
- You can also start from a fresh blank save without picking a file.

## Better replays
- **New playback controls:** a timeline you can click or drag to skip anywhere, 10-second jump buttons and playback speed from 25% to 400%.
- **Bookmarks:** mark your favorite moments. They're saved inside the replay file.
- **Faster video export,** with the option to show chat in the exported video.
- **Faster catch-up** when you start watching a live match partway through.
- Spectators now see the right player names, even when people join or leave mid-match.
- Everyone in the room when a game starts can save a replay of it.

releases.name: BOTWRecompAndroid 0.4.8 (beta 40): caçando o travamento, e texturas sem esperas
releases.body:
**Beta 40.** Correções para threads do jogo que podiam ficar esperando para sempre, um relatório de travamento que mostra onde a thread principal do jogo está, e trocas de textura sem esperar a thread de render em toda GPU.

## O travamento depois de alguns minutos (#401, #489)

Os primeiros logs da 0.4.7 mostraram que **não é a GPU**: quando trava, a thread principal do jogo segura o "núcleo 0" (o app faz as threads desse núcleo se revezarem, como no Switch) e não larga, enquanto as outras esperam. Uma delas pediu para dormir 100 ms e ficou 10 s esperando atrás dela.

- **Relatório de travamento:** além da lista de threads, o log agora diz quem segura o núcleo 0, há quanto tempo, quem está na fila, e onde a thread que o segura está naquele momento. Quem tem o travamento: espere uns 15 s depois de travar, feche o app e mande o `botwrecomp-log-previous.txt` (Configurações > Arquivos).
- **Três correções que podiam deixar uma thread do jogo esperando para sempre:**

releases.name: BOTWRecompAndroid 0.4.7 (beta 39): mapa certo com a Economia de RAM, opção de sombras e menos esperas por shaders
releases.body:
**Beta 39.** O mapa e o minimapa não ficam mais escuros com a Economia de RAM ligada, chega a opção Vídeo > Sombras, e o jogo espera menos por shaders. Várias mudanças vieram de colaboradores (obrigado, Propinbo e HallanBR!).

## Correções

- **Mapa e minimapa escuros com a "Economia de RAM" ligada (#471, #478):** com o zoom no mapa, ou no minimapa, a imagem ficava escura.
  - **Causa:** com a Economia de RAM, depois de enviar uma textura à GPU o app devolvia a memória dela ao Android, e essa memória passava a ler zeros. Mas o jogo às vezes cria a textura de novo sobre a mesma memória sem carregar o arquivo outra vez, e ela era enviada a partir dos zeros.
  - **Agora:** a memória vai para o swap do Android com o conteúdo guardado: a economia continua, e nada vira zero. Se você tinha o problema, conte se resolveu.
- **Frame rate 40 / 45 em telas de 120 Hz (#455):** o HyperOS deixa o jogo em 60 Hz até ele pedir mais, e o modo caía para 30. Agora o app pergunta ao Android a maior taxa que a tela oferece e pede 120 Hz. Contribuição do HallanBR.

## Novidades

releases.name: BOTWRecompAndroid 0.4.6 (beta 38): a água tem colisão de novo, e menos lentidão depois de carregar
releases.body:
**Beta 38.** O Link não atravessa mais a água dos rios depois de um tempo jogando, o jogo volta à velocidade normal 1 s depois de cada carregamento, e vários fechamentos foram corrigidos. Várias correções vieram de colaboradores (obrigado, Propinbo!).

## Correções

- **Água sem colisão depois de um tempo (#296, #438):** depois de 30-60 min, o Link afundava nos rios e andava no fundo, com a água ainda desenhada por cima. Só reiniciar o app resolvia.
  - **Causa:** um pedaço da textura de altura da água era recriado em branco e escrito de volta por cima do que o jogo usa para a colisão.
  - **Agora:** o conteúdo é carregado antes. Correção do Propinbo (#461).
- **Lento por ~10 s depois de cada carregamento (#465):** depois de carregar o save ou de uma viagem rápida, o "Sync lag" (Vídeo) ficava desligado por 300 quadros. Em GPUs mais fracas isso eram ~12 s a 17-20 fps.
  - **Agora:** ele volta depois de 1 s. A água continua certa (era o motivo da espera longa); conferido na torre do Grande Platô.

releases.name: BOTWRecompAndroid 0.4.5 (beta 37): menos memória presa e melhorias vindas do TOTK
releases.body:
**Beta 37.** Os shaders do jogo deixam de ficar para sempre na memória, o FXAA ficou mais leve, e chegam quatro melhorias do [TOTKDroid](https://github.com/mamcjr/TOTKDroid): o relógio do modo Nativo nos aparelhos MediaTek, mais dois efeitos de áudio do jogo, e texturas e vértices no modo cópia (Mali, Xclipse).

## Memória

- **Shaders liberados ao reiniciar o jogo:** cada vez que o jogo era reiniciado ou voltava à tela inicial pelo menu do app, ficavam na memória todos os shaders e pipelines já montados. Agora eles são liberados. Num teste com 16 trocas de cena, a memória terminou em 1075 MB em vez de 1646 MB.
- **Shaders sem uso liberados na Mali e nas outras GPUs não Adreno (#450):** os shaders nunca eram liberados durante o jogo (1513 vivos depois de 30 min, quando uma Mali-G720 fechou no limite de memória do Android). Agora, passados de 1000, os que ficaram 10 min (depois 3 min) sem uso são liberados e montados de novo quando o jogo voltar a usá-los. Deve reduzir os fechamentos em sessões longas na Mali, mas ainda falta confirmar num aparelho Mali: se você tinha esse problema, conte se melhorou.

## Vindo do TOTK

releases.name: BOTWRecompAndroid 0.4.4 (beta 36): sem queda de fps depois dos menus
releases.body:
# BOTWRecompAndroid 0.4.4 (beta 36): sem queda de fps depois dos menus

**Beta 36.** O jogo volta à velocidade normal logo depois de um menu, e a geração de quadros chega a mais GPUs Mali.

## Correções

- **Queda de fps depois de qualquer menu (#374, #439, #433):** por uns 12 s depois de fechar o menu de pausa, o inventário ou a troca de runas, o jogo ficava em 20-27 fps e depois voltava ao normal.
  - **Causa:** ao fechar o menu, o app desligava o "Sync lag" (Vídeo) por 300 quadros, como depois de uma tela de carregamento.
  - **Agora:** o menu não conta mais como saída do mundo. No POCO F7 Ultra, os trechos de 2 s abaixo de 29 fps depois dos menus caíram de 12 para 0.
- **Preso em 20 fps depois de um engasgo:** um engasgo isolado (save, menu, shaders compilando) não leva mais o jogo para 20 fps. E, se ele estiver em 20 fps, tenta voltar a 30 a cada poucos segundos, em vez de esperar o trabalho por quadro cair muito.
- **Geração de quadros: "no Lossless.dll" com o arquivo no lugar certo (#437, #385):** o Android mostra o arquivo em Download/ para o app, mas não deixa abrir sem a permissão de acesso a todos os arquivos.

Unreal Tournament 3 Android ARM64 port, version 0.5-dev (versionCode 9).

### Changes

- Added native implementations of selected game, rendering, AI and container algorithms, with the original recompiled paths retained. Optimized guest-register handling, x87 calculations and indirect-call caches.
- Added Optimal (ARM64) and Exact (x86) execution modes. Exact selects the original recompiled algorithms; both modes run as ARM64 code.
- Reduced GLES state traffic between threads, draw preparation work and shader constant uploads, and improved shader program caching.
- Improved launcher operation progress, diagnostics and Play button feedback, with the amber UT3 palette.
- Added an optional 4 GB guest address space, enabled by default on 64-bit devices with at least 5 GiB of RAM.
- Fixed fingerprint sensors being mistaken for gamepads.
- Reduced APK size by stripping non-runtime library symbols while retaining the original library for offline profiling. Expanded regression tests and updated documentation.

### Requirements

releases.body:
Unreal Tournament 3 Android ARM64 port, version 0.4.1-dev (versionCode 8).

### Changes

- Improved CPU performance on PhysX Mod Pack maps with native fluid collision kernels, native pair removal and optimized x87 calculations.
- Added on-device HLSL compilation through vkd3d-shader, with shader caching and improved MojoShader compatibility for mod materials.
- Fixed touch aiming: holding Fire no longer blocks another finger's camera movement; dragging from Fire, secondary fire, Jump or Crouch also turns the camera.
- Made the crash monitor a launcher option, disabled by default, to avoid keeping its extra Android process running unless needed.
- Removed FSR3 frame generation. FSR1 spatial upscaling and FXAA remain available.
- Reduced per-draw post-processing overhead and removed temporary qa-flags performance switches.
- Updated localized PhysX and audio setting descriptions.

### Installation and validation

Requires Android 11+ on ARM64 and your own files from the Steam version of the game. DXVK requires Vulkan 1.3; compatible Adreno devices can use Turnip.

releases.name: Unreal Tournament 3 Android ARM64 port 0.4-dev
releases.body:
Unreal Tournament 3 Android ARM64 port, version 0.4-dev.

### Changes

- Added an FPS counter with a frame-time graph and optional system information for every renderer.
- Added FSR1, FXAA, and FSR3.1 frame generation (DXVK, Android 12+; disabled by default).
- Added CPU-based PhysX effects and OpenAL Soft audio through AAudio with EAX 1–5 support.
- Added a maximum-graphics button and fixed persistence of the 3D rendering scale.
- Fixed terrain rendering in OpenGL ES, accelerated DXT decoding, and allowed unused texture mip levels to stream out.
- Improved GPU query handling in GLES and DXVK, including on PowerVR devices.
- Fixed ASTC/ETC2 texture conversion on shared storage on Pixel devices.
- Added a “Firing or aiming” gyroscope mode and persistent crash reports with a separate error window.

### Installation and limitations

Requires Android 11+ on ARM64 and your own files from the Steam version of the game. DXVK requires Vulkan 1.3; frame generation requires Android 12+. Frame generation may cause HUD artifacts and adds GPU and memory overhead. A stable 60 FPS at maximum graphics settings is not guaranteed.

releases.name: Unreal Tournament 3 Android ARM64 port 0.3-dev
releases.body:
The third release of the native Android ARM64 port of Unreal Tournament 3 improves GLES performance, text editing and graphics cache handling.

### Changes

- Added a dedicated GLES render thread with automatic CPU core selection. Streamed draw uploads, asynchronous query polling and shader program prelinking reduce work on the game thread.
- Added driver-aware graphics cache maintenance: GLES program binaries are invalidated after driver changes, and DXVK keeps the current and newest other pipeline cache for each driver.
- Fixed DXVK scaled vertex formats with a shader fallback for drivers that need it.
- Replaced keyboard-only text entry with an Android editing dialog for game fields, console commands and chat. Existing text can be corrected or cleared; cancellation preserves it, and original character filters remain in effect.
- Added separate weapon-button swipe settings and expanded the in-game Android settings to nine languages: English, Russian, Czech, German, Spanish, French, Hungarian, Italian and Polish.
- Improved launcher texture status and fixed texture handling, audio and FSINCOS translation. Expanded regression tests and rendering diagnostics.

### Requirements

releases.name: v0.4.7
releases.body:
Phones get new defaults that run smoother and cooler, voices on Android should come through again, and every platform gets a Render scale option. Everything from [0.4.6](https://github.com/santiquiroz/gears-of-war-2-pc-port/releases/tag/v0.4.6) is included.

## Android

- **Frame rate unlocked with a 45 fps limit, by default.** Uncapped, the phone's GPU runs at full load until the phone lowers its clock as it heats up; the limit keeps headroom. The limit drops to the nearest rate that divides your screen's refresh, so every frame lasts the same: 40 fps on a 120 Hz screen (Galaxy S24/S25), 45 at 90 Hz, 30 at 60 Hz. On an S25 Ultra frame times went from a 25/25/16.7 ms mix to an even 25 ms. You can still pick 30, 60 or no limit in Device Options > Display > Frame rate limit.
- **Render scale 75 % by default.** The 3D scene is drawn at 75 % and scaled up to the screen; on an S25 Ultra that is 14 % less GPU work per frame, with a slightly softer picture. Graphics > Render scale goes back to 100 %.
- **Snapdragon GSR for the final upscale by default**, one pass instead of FSR 1's two.

releases.name: v0.4.6
releases.body:
Insane can now be picked from the start. Everything from [0.4.5](https://github.com/santiquiroz/gears-of-war-2-pc-port/releases/tag/v0.4.5) is included; if you have not read its notes, they cover the Riftworm fix for Vulkan, GPU detection on Linux and Proton, and the co-op go-to-player-1 key.

## Every platform

- **Insane without finishing the campaign first.** The option from 0.4.5, now named **All chapters and Insane unlocked** (PC Options > Saves, on by default), also enables the Insane button in the difficulty menu, in solo Campaign and in the co-op lobby. Before, the game greyed it out until the campaign had been finished once. As with chapters, only the menu check changes: your saved progress and the Extras list of unlockables are not touched.

## Known, still open

- Lighting that looks pixelated on Linux with presets above Low, and black textures on Low on Windows (both on a Legion Go): we could not reproduce them on our PC. A screenshot and the `logs/gow2_*.log` of the run, with the chapter, help a lot.

releases.name: v0.4.5
releases.body:
The Riftworm interior no longer crashes or goes black with Vulkan, the game picks the right GPU settings on Linux and under Proton, every chapter can be picked from the start, and co-op gets a key and a controller combo to go to player 1. Everything from [0.4.4](https://github.com/santiquiroz/gears-of-war-2-pc-port/releases/tag/v0.4.4) is included.

## Vulkan (Linux and SteamOS, Proton with Vulkan, Android, Vulkan on Windows)

- **Inside the Riftworm (act 5) no longer loses the GPU.** The worm's flesh is drawn with tessellation, and the shaders the renderer builds for it read their settings from the wrong slot, so the tessellation factor came from unrelated memory: the scene stayed black, would not load, or the game closed with a lost device. Fixed in SDK patch 0091 (found with the Khronos validation layer). On a Radeon RX 7800 XT the worm interior now runs 120 s at 60 fps where it failed within seconds. Under Proton, Vulkan (`gpu_backend = vulkan`) is the backend to use for that chapter: D3D12 through vkd3d-proton was also reported to lose the device there and we could not test it.

## Linux and SteamOS

releases.name: v0.4.4
releases.body:
Less memory traffic on phone GPUs, less work per draw on the GPU command thread, and a new option for the CPU core the game spins while it waits for the GPU. Everything from [0.4.3](https://github.com/santiquiroz/gears-of-war-2-pc-port/releases/tag/v0.4.3) is included.

## Vulkan (Android, Linux and SteamOS, Vulkan on Windows)

- **Each render pass now covers only what it draws.** The renderer sizes its render targets for the console's whole EDRAM (1520x3456 on the phone) and every render pass loaded and stored all of it, even when its draws touched only the 1280x720 of a 720p frame. Phone GPUs render in tiles and pay for every byte a pass loads and stores, so they moved about 5.7 times the memory they needed. Now each pass begins with only the area its draws and clears can write (SDK patch 0089). It follows the Vulkan rules, so the picture should not change; it has not been measured on a phone yet. If part of the picture looks missing or stale, set `vulkan_tight_render_area = false` in `gow2.toml` (it takes effect at once) and open an issue with the scene. Direct3D 12, the Windows default, is not affected.

## Every platform

releases.name: v0.4.3
releases.body:
A new Android APK that survives leaving the game, a leaner game binary on every platform, and threads that sleep instead of polling on Linux and Android. Everything from [0.4.2](https://github.com/santiquiroz/gears-of-war-2-pc-port/releases/tag/v0.4.2) is included.

## Android

- **Leaving the game and coming back no longer crashes it.** Home, switching to another app or the screen turning off, then coming back: up to 0.3.18 the return crashed (in `vkCreateAndroidSurfaceKHR`, with a window Android had already freed). Now the game lets go of the old window when it leaves the screen and connects to the new one when it comes back (SDK patch 0085). The game keeps running while it is off screen (only the picture and the sound stop), so pause it before you leave.
- **The update dialog holds the game until you answer it**, instead of letting it start behind the dialog, and the phone only offers releases that carry an APK (0.4.2 was for PC and Linux only).

releases.name: shadps4 v0.18.0 - codename UltraPersona
releases.body:
shadPS4 v0.18.0 "UltraPersona"

Hello there, it hasn't been a while, has it? While not much time has passed since our last stable release, we are here again with a brand new one. The main reason for this release is broken shadNet authorization in certain cases on the 0.17.0 release, but we have some more interesting new features as well.

Firstly, after some fixes, AvPlayer can now be loaded as LLE, meaning that you need the `libSceAvPlayer.sprx` (and `libSceAvPlayerStreaming.sprx`) module(s), which makes broken videos in a few games now work properly.

The above change was enabled by calling `sceLibcInternalMemoryMutexEnable` in LLE LibcInternal at boot, found by [@liuk7071](https://github.com/liuk7071), the developer of ChonkyStation4, another PS4 emulator.

A kernel event flag rewrite has also fixed Shadow of the Colossus often hanging on boot, and the game now consistently gets to menus.

releases.name: RunnerBuilder 0.3.3
releases.body:
Builds your own Android APK of the PC version from your own copy of Mirror's Edge from GOG. Other releases of the game do not work.

**New in 0.3.3: much faster.**
- Before the build the program asks where the result goes: a device over USB or Wi-Fi debugging, or a folder only. With a device, the game files are copied to it **while** the game's code is being built, and the finished app is installed at the end. No ZIP is made then.
- A first build takes about 5 minutes on a fast PC (was about 10): the translation runs in parallel and a 2-3 minute stall at the end of every build is gone.
- The build is kept: after an update of the program it takes a minute or two instead of starting over.
- The window is sharp on screens scaled to 125-200%.
- App 0.3.3: no more 1-second freezes when the game restarts its rendering thread (a sleep in the game's own code, skipped); PlayStation button icons when a DualSense is connected during play; a clear message while the game's code is still being built.

Tested on one PC and a Lenovo Y700: a full build with install over Wi-Fi in about 5 minutes. **Not tested yet:** the full 11.5 GB copy during a build, USB, the 1-second freeze fix in long play.

# NSP Box 4.0.0 — Meet NUP

Smaller archives, flexible packaging, and more control over your game collection. Version 4.0 introduces **NUP Tools**, alongside the existing NSP builder.

### Package more. Store less.

- **Create compressed NUP archives** from extracted game folders, with base games, updates and DLC together in one file.
- **Choose your balance:** Fast for quicker compression, Balanced for everyday use, or Smaller for stronger compression. Incompressible files are stored raw automatically.
- **Keep what you need:** select Base, Updates and DLC independently. Choices appear after inspection, only for content present in your source. Latest-snapshot mode merges the newest selected update with the selected base, retains required base-only files, and leaves superseded versions behind. Turn it off to keep separate base/update records.
- **Avoid duplicate storage:** identical file contents can share the same space inside an archive.
- **Stay compatible:** leave files larger than 256 MiB uncompressed to reduce temporary decompression work in supported emulators.

### Convert, extract and check

- **NSP → NUP:** compress plaintext NSPs created by NSP Box.

releases.name: Version 5.10.1
releases.body:
Changes:

* `install`, `push`: better handling for registry rate limits (HTTP 429) by honoring `Retry-After`, show detailed error when rate limit occurs while using a shared Docker Hub frontend (proxy) instead of raw `Network error: HTTP Error 429`.

Notice for users: this does not resolve issue with rate limits imposed by Docker Hub registry. Such issue just can't be resolved at proot-distro side because restriction applies to client IP address, which in case of NAT (CG-NAT) or proxy may be shared between large amount of devices.

Don't submit bug reports if encounter HTTP 429!

Workaround:

1. Create Docker Hub account.
2. Use `export PD_DOCKER_AUTH="username:password"` or `export PD_DOCKER_AUTH="username:personal-access-token"`, the personal access token must be created through account settings with permissions at least for read-only access.

releases.name: Version 5.10.0
releases.body:
Changes:

- refs: Image names are now checked using Docker's rules. Malformed names are refused with a clear message.
- install: Added support for images pinned by digest, e.g. `ubuntu@sha256:...`. The download is verified against the digest. A pinned image can be reinstalled from the cache without network.
- build, push: A digest is refused in `build -t` and `push`.
- install: Fixed intact image layers sometimes refused with "does not match its digest".
- http: Redirects can no longer move a download from HTTPS to plain HTTP. `--allow-insecure` lifts this.
- registry: `--allow-insecure` no longer applies to Docker Hub. It is always verified.
- http: Network requests give up after 2 minutes of silence instead of hanging forever.
- http: Invalid URLs and registry addresses now show an error message instead of a traceback.
- build, login: Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 in arguments, build args or image environment no longer cause a traceback.
- list, remove: `--image` no longer prints control characters from cache entries as they are.
- sync, copy: Files that change during the transfer are handled correctly. No more missed updates or wrong permissions.

releases.name: Version 5.9.0
releases.body:
Changes:

- `login`, `run`: export variables `PD_CONTAINER=<name>`, `PD_IMAGE=<image-ref>`, `PD_IMAGE_ID=<sha256-digest>` and `container=proot-distro` in sessions. Build gets same except `PD_CONTAINER`.
- `pull`: detect whether image config or manifest is shorter than `Content-Length`.
- `build` (ADD, COPY): placing directory over an existing regular file is now a refusal instead of a silent tree/layer mismatch.
- `build` (... --chmod): validate value as an octal between 0 and 07777.
- `build`: Dockerfile is read with 16 MiB limit.
- `push`: send the Bearer token on the upload PUT only when the Location URL belongs to the registry itself.
- Registry credentials are only sent to the origin they were addressed to.
- Do not carry Authorization header if host redirects from HTTPS to HTTP.
- A token endpoint realm must be `https://` (`http://` allowed under --allow-insecure). `file://`, `ftp://` and `data:` realms are refused.
- Environment strings from image config are validated before exec (no NUL, encodable, under 128 KiB).
- The `profile.d` snippet is written for every session of a normal-type container, not only default-mode Termux logins.

NgpCraft Emulator v3.9.0 - what's new
This release is about playing two players over the internet. It is still being tested, but the
first results are encouraging. If you play online, both of you should update, and please tell us
how it goes.

Online play in mirror mode should be smoother
Less input lag at the start of a match. The player who finished loading first used to start alone and wait for the other one. That wait made the emulator think the connection was slower than it really was, and it could add noticeable delay to that player's controls for several minutes. Both sides now start together. This idea comes from Blueteemo, who proposed it in pull request #26. Thank you!
Fewer freezes on a connection that loses packets. Your button presses are now also sent a second way, repeated several times, so a single lost packet should no longer freeze both screens. In our tests on a deliberately bad connection, most of the short freezes went away.
If the other player has an older version, the match should still work, just without these improvements.

releases.name: Version 0.30.6
releases.body:
# Skyrim for Android 0.30.6

APK: `Skyrim-0.30.6.apk` (arm64-v8a, Android 9+, Vulkan 1.1).

## New
- "Disable end-of-frame image space (post-processing)" option. It does the same as the TEOFIS console command at every launch. It fixes the black world map and solid-colour underwater screen, but it also turns off all end-of-frame post-processing (tonemapping, bloom, colour grading and depth of field), so the game looks more naturally lit.
- "Asynchronous rendering" option. It's off by default and when it's on, shaders compile on background threads. New effects may pop in for a frame or two instead of causing a hitch. 

## Fixed
- Shader caching is removed. The DXVK state cache rebuilt every saved pipeline on 5 extra threads at startup, which took CPU away from the game's main thread and caused crashes on Mali devices. Nothing is cached between launches now, and the game runs better overall.
- Traps triggering freezes was due to failed lookups with vertex optimization. The function has been turned off for now.
- Audio in other languages - the decoder was reading each WMA bitstream but with the wrong block-size config. Should be working now.

WinCore 5.0.0 — Compatibility Suite

WinCore 5.0.0 introduces a major expansion of the WinCore Compatibility Center, bringing 50 diagnostic and compatibility tools for Windows games running through Winlator.

What's New

Compatibility Center

- 50 numbered compatibility and diagnostic actions.
- Windows executable and game-folder inspection.
- Local compatibility database.
- Advisory compatibility profiles.
- Wine, Box64, and graphics configuration recommendations.
- Per-game profile history and JSON import/export.

GTA IV Diagnostics

- GTA IV profile setup.
- Executable and component checks.
- Save-data filename inspection.
- Compatibility summaries and troubleshooting information.

Device and Performance Diagnostics

- RAM and thermal snapshots.
- CPU timing information.
- Launch-readiness checks.
- Android controller and audio-device inspection.

Logs and Troubleshooting

- Wine and Box64 log filtering.
- Missing-DLL pattern detection.
- Custom compatibility rules.
- Folder and component checks.
- Diagnostic reports.

Branding

- Updated WinCore green four-panel application icon.
- Matching WinCore logo across branding resources.

releases.name: WinCore 4.0.0
releases.body:
WinCore 4.0.0 — App Icon Issue

WinCore 4.0.0 was released without the intended WinCore app icon because of an error during the GitHub release/build process. The supplied artwork was not correctly integrated into the APK, leaving the release without the proper WinCore branding.
This issue was addressed in WinCore 5.0.0, which includes the updated green four-panel app icon and logo, with automated checks confirming the branding resources were included.

releases.name: WinCore 3.0.0
releases.body:
WinCore 3.0.0 expands Android device-profile customization with per-game and per-container CPU profile overrides, configurable Box64 mappings, and automatic chipset-family detection.

This release introduces adaptive launch safety for low-memory and severe thermal conditions, an optional live session monitor, JSON device-profile sharing, and appearance reset.

Existing Winlator container management, game shortcuts, graphics settings, controller support, and compatibility diagnostics are preserved.

Note: CI verifies the build and APK integrity. Actual game compatibility and performance have not been verified on physical devices.

releases.name: WinCore 2.0.0
releases.body:
WinCore 2.0.0 introduces automatic chipset-family detection for common Dimensity, Snapdragon, and Exynos devices, with selectable device profiles applied through Box64 when launching Windows programs.

This release also adds eight app-wide accent color options and three interface sizes: Compact, Standard, and Large. Existing Winlator containers, shortcuts, settings, controller navigation, and read-only compatibility diagnostics are preserved.

Note: chipset-to-profile mappings are baseline defaults and have not been benchmark-verified.
